topic: Censoring-robust spectral synthetic survival control under covariate-dependent right censoring.

open_problems.open_problem: Can Han and Shah's rank-r synthetic survival control have valid joint root-K inference when every fixed panel-cell survival curve is estimated under covariate-dependent right censoring by one fully specified cross-fitted augmented-IPCW score?

source_refs.claim: SSC identifies a low-rank counterfactual hazard trajectory and gives finite-sample guarantees, but assumes non-informative censoring and explicitly leaves IPCW or joint-model extensions for future work.
source_refs.author: Jessy Xinyi Han and Devavrat Shah

source_refs.claim: Constructs a cross-fitted doubly robust survival-curve estimator under conditional censoring and proves pointwise and uniform asymptotic linearity with data-adaptive nuisances.
source_refs.author: Ted Westling, Alex Luedtke, Peter B. Gilbert, and Marco Carone
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Analyzes PCR in a fixed-design errors-in-variables problem and gives row-space out-of-sample prediction guarantees, without censoring-aware influence-function inference.
source_refs.author: Anish Agarwal, Devavrat Shah, and Dennis Shen

open_problems.why_unsolved: The sources stop on opposite sides of the required composition. Han and Shah explicitly flag their non-informative-censoring boundary, while Westling et al. establish an orthogonal survival expansion for one target but do not stack many cell-by-time estimates and pass their estimated influence vectors through a data-dependent rank-r PCR map. The first unresolved step is to fix a right-continuous/left-continuous tie convention and show that the cross-fitted cellwise second-order remainder is O_p(a_K b_K)+o_p(K^-1/2), jointly over all fixed cells and times, with no uncancelled first-order censoring or event-survival nuisance term. Only then can the full derivative of (y,M,B) ↦ yM_r^+B, including both projector correction terms, yield the joint influence vector; the visible literature does not contain this composition.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A joint root-K asymptotic-linear representation with an explicit influence vector for the J-dimensional untreated curve, L2-consistent estimated influence vectors, a consistent covariance estimator, a valid Gaussian-multiplier simultaneous grid band, and a studentized grid-RMST contrast limit.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the destination estimand, low-rank panel-survival formulation, and the 925-patient, 10-country TCL motivation while stating the informative-censoring limitation directly.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: TCL treatment adoption is staggered across countries -> SSC transports low-rank donor survival information to the untreated US counterfactual -> covariate-dependent censoring makes that clinical curve require orthogonal estimation and simultaneous uncertainty quantification.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the explicit cross-fitted one-step survival score, its product-form nuisance-remainder proof, estimated-influence consistency, and uniform weak-convergence argument as the cellwise first stage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each panel cell asks for the same marginal survival functional under conditional independent censoring; the new work is joint stacking and spectral propagation.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the constant-rank Fréchet derivative of the Moore-Penrose inverse, including both orthogonal-projector correction terms, and apply the product rule to yM_r^+B.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The counterfactual is exactly a smooth vector functional of a constant-rank pseudoinverse once the cell estimates have a joint influence expansion.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply Gaussian comparison, anti-concentration, and conditional Gaussian multipliers to the maximum of the estimated transported influence-vector coordinates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The simultaneous J-grid statistic is a maximum of normalized sums of influence vectors, the object controlled by their multiplier-bootstrap machinery.

open_problems.open_problem: For exact donor-span survival panels with covariate-dependent censoring, when does unadjusted cellwise Kaplan-Meier followed by rank-r PCR have a nonzero fixed counterfactual-curve bias, and what exceptional cancellation conditions make that bias vanish?

source_refs.claim: Shows that linear synthetic controls generally bias expected survival and survival curves under common survival data-generating processes.
source_refs.author: Alicia Curth, Hoifung Poon, Aditya V. Nori, and Javier González
source_refs.venue: Conference on Causal Learning and Reasoning, PMLR 236

source_refs.claim: Explains that event-censoring dependence makes Kaplan-Meier inconsistent even after treatment randomization, while covariate adjustment permits conditional independent censoring.
source_refs.author: Ted Westling, Alex Luedtke, Peter B. Gilbert, and Marco Carone
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Builds the untreated trajectory by low-rank spectral donor transport but assumes non-informative censoring in its theoretical treatment.
source_refs.author: Jessy Xinyi Han and Devavrat Shah

open_problems.why_unsolved: Westling et al. isolate marginal Kaplan-Meier inconsistency under dependent censoring, and Curth et al. isolate distributional failures of survival synthetic controls, but neither characterizes how cell-specific Kaplan-Meier pseudo-limits enter all three learned PCR blocks. The first missing step is to derive the population Kaplan-Meier limit under conditional-but-not-marginal independent censoring and substitute its perturbations into the treated pre-row, donor pre-matrix, and donor post-matrix simultaneously. Exact donor-span transport for the true curves does not prevent those three deterministic biases from being mixed or, on exceptional lower-dimensional sets, cancelled by the pseudoinverse.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient population cancellation condition plus an explicit open subclass of event/censoring laws on which the KM/PCR counterfactual curve, and therefore its grid-RMST, differs from the true untreated target by a fixed nonzero vector.

writing_exemplar.why: Its cautionary arc turns a plausible survival-control workflow into a precise structural failure mechanism and is the closest framing for a sharp nonrobustness result.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Synthetic controls appear natural for sparse survival comparisons -> survival distributions and censoring violate assumptions hidden by scalar-outcome intuition -> identify a stable observable regime where KM/PCR converges to the wrong curve.

method_exemplars.technique: Use its observed-data product-integral formulation to express the unadjusted Kaplan-Meier pseudo-target and contrast it with the covariate-adjusted marginal survival functional.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The deterministic perturbation entering PCR is exactly the gap between those two survival functionals.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the minimum-norm PCR and row-space characterization to propagate deterministic misspecification across pre and post blocks.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After taking Kaplan-Meier probability limits, the remaining problem is deterministic misspecified PCR transport in the geometry this paper analyzes.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the sharp inference phase transition for censoring-robust spectral synthetic survival control when the rank-r singular gap shrinks with K and the working rank may be overestimated or data-selected?

source_refs.excerpt: The only inverse-gap step is the transport-to-label inequality (11); the quotient-law risk (3) remains gap-free.

source_refs.claim: SSC uses a rank-truncated low-rank construction with a well-conditioned spectral regime and does not give weak-gap or rank-selection inference.
source_refs.author: Jessy Xinyi Han and Devavrat Shah

source_refs.claim: Gives inference for linear functionals of high-dimensional low-rank matrices without consistent rank estimation and identifies non-negligible bias from rank overestimation.
source_refs.author: Jungjun Choi, Hyukjun Kwon, and Yuan Liao
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior CausalSmith construction proves that an invariant quotient can remain gap-free while labeled coordinates incur inverse-gap loss, making it unclear which side the composite prediction yM_r^+B occupies near a collision. The web literature resolves rank overestimation for linear functionals of large low-rank matrices using diversified projections, but the survival counterfactual is a nonlinear pseudoinverse functional of several cross-fitted cell blocks in a fixed-panel, large-within-cell regime. The fixed-gap derivative can diverge or cease to be continuous when the gap reaches the K^-1/2 perturbation scale; the first missing step is a uniform expansion or a two-path local impossibility construction that accounts jointly for rank selection and censoring-score noise.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Matching upper and lower risk bounds indexed by (K,Δ_K), with regular, critical, and nonregular regimes, plus either a uniformly valid band under rank overestimation/data selection or a sharp impossibility statement below the critical gap scale.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents the applied rank-truncated SSC workflow whose well-conditioned-spectrum boundary creates the opportunity.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Spectral truncation stabilizes noisy survival panels -> practical ranks are selected and weak factors are unavoidable -> inference must either survive rank uncertainty or mark a sharp nonregular boundary.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt diversified projections, the bias correction for overestimated rank, and the uniform CLT for low-rank linear functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly treats rank misspecification; the transfer must replace its linear functional by the multi-block spectral survival prediction.

method_exemplars.technique: Track the constant-rank pseudoinverse derivative and its remainder explicitly as the gap shrinks, then identify which projector terms cancel in yM_r^+B.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The candidate critical rate is controlled by the derivative and remainder norms of the exact composite map.

method_exemplars.technique: Retain the orthogonal cross-fitted cell score so weak spectral identification is separated from first-order nuisance bias.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A local weak-gap experiment needs a regular cell-level noise representation before spectral nonregularity can be isolated.

open_problems.open_problem: Can fixed-grid censoring-robust spectral synthetic survival control be lifted to a continuous-time counterfactual survival process with uniform root-K inference and a continuous, rather than grid-discretized, RMST effect?

source_refs.claim: Proves uniform-in-time asymptotic linearity for a cross-fitted doubly robust survival curve and supports inference for integrated curve contrasts.
source_refs.author: Ted Westling, Alex Luedtke, Peter B. Gilbert, and Marco Carone
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Develops synthetic controls for function- and metric-space-valued outcomes through Hilbert-space embeddings, with finite-sample bounds and prediction sets but no censoring-robust influence-process inference.
source_refs.author: Ryo Okano and Daisuke Kurisu

source_refs.claim: Defines a low-rank counterfactual survival/hazard trajectory but does not derive a censoring-robust functional weak limit for the learned spectral map.
source_refs.author: Jessy Xinyi Han and Devavrat Shah

open_problems.why_unsolved: Westling et al. supply a continuous-time weak limit for one survival functional, while Okano and Kurisu supply functional-outcome synthetic-control geometry without right-censoring nuisances; neither differentiates a spectral donor map whose entries are estimated survival processes. The first proof step that changes from the fixed-grid case is replacing an ordinary multivariate delta method by Hadamard/Fréchet differentiability from a product of càdlàg-function spaces into ℓ∞ on the horizon, while controlling tail positivity, stochastic equicontinuity, and integration error. Targeted searches did not locate this right-censoring/AIPCW/functional-synthetic-control combination.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A functional asymptotic-linear expansion and tight Gaussian-process limit in ℓ∞ on a prespecified horizon, with a uniformly valid curve band and an integrated influence-function CLT for the continuous-time RMST effect.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames why curve-valued outcomes require functional synthetic-control theory rather than unrelated scalar fits.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Policy outcomes can be whole functions rather than scalars -> ordinary synthetic-control algebra does not automatically supply functional inference -> survival curves add censoring and require a transported process-level limit.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the uniform cross-fitted influence process, tightness proof for mixed discrete/continuous event times, band construction, and integration of the influence function.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It establishes the exact cell-level functional limit required before applying synthetic-control transport.

method_exemplars.technique: Lift the constant-rank pseudoinverse derivative to operator coefficients acting continuously on the product function space.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is still produced by a constant-rank pseudoinverse, but its perturbations now range over a time-indexed Banach space.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Gaussian coupling and multiplier-bootstrap approximation for suprema of empirical processes to calibrate the continuous-time band.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The inferential target is the supremum of a transported influence process rather than a fixed coordinate maximum.

open_problems.open_problem: Under what structural conditions do linear-span, Wasserstein/quantile, and Hilbert-embedded synthetic controls identify the same untreated survival distribution, and when does one geometry identify it while another necessarily fails?

source_refs.claim: Identifies a counterfactual survival/hazard trajectory through a low-rank linear donor-span restriction.
source_refs.author: Jessy Xinyi Han and Devavrat Shah

source_refs.claim: Shows that linear synthetic individuals can distort survival means and curves because their induced distributions have the wrong variance and shape.
source_refs.author: Alicia Curth, Hoifung Poon, Aditya V. Nori, and Javier González
source_refs.venue: Conference on Causal Learning and Reasoning, PMLR 236

source_refs.claim: Identifies a unique counterfactual quantile function by synthesizing donor quantile functions in Wasserstein geometry.
source_refs.author: Florian F. Gunsilius

source_refs.claim: Uses isometric Hilbert-space embeddings to extend synthetic controls to metric-space-valued distributions and functions.
source_refs.author: Ryo Okano and Daisuke Kurisu

open_problems.why_unsolved: The sources create a concrete identification tension: Han and Shah impose linear span after a survival/hazard representation, Curth et al. show that individual-level linear synthesis can distort the desired survival law, and Gunsilius plus Okano-Kurisu use nonlinear distributional or embedded geometries. None supplies correspondence conditions among these model classes. The first proof step is to compare the donor-span restrictions themselves—determining when a linear combination of survival functions is the image of the same latent transport as a Wasserstein barycenter or Hilbert embedding—and to construct separation examples when the restrictions disagree.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient correspondence characterization for equality of the three counterfactual functionals, explicit data-generating regimes identified under exactly one geometry, and an estimable diagnostic for the correspondence condition under censoring.

writing_exemplar.why: It most clearly turns ambiguity about what a synthetic survival unit represents into an identification question.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Linear synthetic controls work well for scalar panels -> survival targets are distributions whose shape can be altered by synthesis -> determine which donor geometry recovers the intended untreated survival law.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the quantile-function/Wasserstein barycenter argument and its distance-preserving causal model to characterize distributional donor transport.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its identified object is the entire counterfactual distribution, which is equivalent to a survival curve after monotone transformation.

method_exemplars.technique: Use isometric embeddings and latent-Hilbert factor restrictions to place survival-function and quantile synthesis in a common comparison space.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a language for comparing otherwise incompatible function and distribution geometries.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate each marginal survival functional with cross-fitted orthogonal scores and derive an influence-process comparison diagnostic.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An empirical geometry diagnostic must first recover survival curves under covariate-dependent censoring without Kaplan-Meier bias.

open_problems.open_problem: Can an observable Gaussian-multiplier band for the fixed-grid spectral synthetic-survival counterfactual remain uniformly honest as its limiting covariance approaches or reaches singularity?

source_refs.excerpt: supplies neither uniform anti-concentration nor an observable common-multiplier coupling through variance degeneracy

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior run obtained population Gaussianization but could not replace a population quadratic quantile by an observable multiplier law uniformly through covariance degeneracy. In the survival-control destination, estimated cell influence vectors must first be propagated through the full pseudoinverse differential and then coupled to the maximum of a Gaussian vector whose covariance may lose rank. Ordinary fixed-law multiplier validity, coordinatewise studentization, and the nondegenerate-covariance theorem contemplated by the current topic do not provide uniform anti-concentration or a correct branch for exactly zero-variance contrasts.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A regime-uniform coverage theorem for a fully observable multiplier band, with consistent critical values and explicit half-width behavior over positive-definite, locally singular, and exactly singular covariance sequences.

writing_exemplar.why: Its clinical curve-estimation problem supplies the reason a band must remain interpretable when some time coordinates or contrasts carry almost no variation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: SSC produces a clinically interpretable counterfactual trajectory -> simultaneous inference is needed across follow-up times -> near-deterministic or redundant coordinates make standard studentized calibration nonuniform.

method_exemplars.technique: Start from Gaussian approximation, multiplier coupling, and anti-concentration for maxima, then isolate which lower-variance conditions fail as covariance loses rank.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired critical value is the conditional quantile of a Gaussian-multiplier maximum, but it must be extended through covariance degeneracy.

method_exemplars.technique: Use estimated survival influence functions and uniform bands as the regular-regime baseline before introducing covariance-rank branches.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the observable influence process whose transported covariance becomes singular in the destination problem.

literature_map:
Han and Shah (2025, arXiv:2511.14133) introduce low-rank Synthetic Survival Control, identify the counterfactual hazard trajectory, and give finite-sample guarantees for the TCL application, but explicitly assume non-informative censoring and name IPCW or joint modeling as future work.
Amjad, Shah, and Shen (2018, JMLR; arXiv:1711.06940) establish robust synthetic control through singular-value thresholding, anchoring the spectral estimator lineage.
Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2025, JMLR; arXiv:2010.14449) characterize minimum-norm PCR and row-space out-of-sample transport, but not censoring-aware limit theory.
Athey, Bayati, Doudchenko, Imbens, and Khosravi (2021, JASA; arXiv:1710.10251) connect causal panels, matrix completion, and low-rank counterfactual imputation.
Westling, Luedtke, Gilbert, and Carone (2024, JASA; arXiv:2106.06602) provide the closest cell-level ingredient: a cross-fitted doubly robust survival curve, nuisance-remainder control, uniform asymptotic linearity, bands, and integrated contrasts.
Chernozhukov et al. (2018, Econometrics Journal; arXiv:1608.00060) supply the general orthogonal-score and cross-fitting logic behind product-rate nuisance control.
Golub and Pereyra (1973, SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis; DOI 10.1137/0710036) give the full constant-rank pseudoinverse derivative needed to propagate treated-pre, donor-pre, and donor-post perturbations.
Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013–2014, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:1212.6906 and 1212.6885) provide multiplier-bootstrap and Gaussian-coupling machinery for grid maxima and process suprema.
Curth, Poon, Nori, and González (2024, CLeaR; arXiv:2312.00501) show that survival synthetic controls can have structural distributional bias under common survival data-generating processes.
Gunsilius (2023, Econometrica; arXiv:2001.06118) offers a competing quantile/Wasserstein geometry for entire counterfactual distributions, creating an identification tension with linear survival-function spans.
Okano and Kurisu (2026, arXiv:2601.07539) develop functional synthetic controls through Hilbert embeddings and prediction sets, but do not address covariate-dependent censoring or orthogonal survival scores.
Lok, Yang, Sharkey, and Hughes (2018, Lifetime Data Analysis; DOI 10.1007/s10985-017-9393-4) derive augmented-IPCW cumulative-incidence estimation under dependent censoring, supplying a route to a later competing-risk SSC extension.
Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2024, Journal of Econometrics; arXiv:2307.16370) develop low-rank completion inference, while their 2026 JASA paper (arXiv:2311.16440) avoids consistent rank estimation via diversified projections.
The strongest unoccupied intersection is orthogonal censoring-robust cell survival estimation composed with a fully differentiated spectral donor map, including simultaneous curve/RMST inference and a sharp naive-KM/PCR failure result.
prior_proposal_map:
The bounded Track-A scan found no prior survival, censoring, IPCW/AIPCW, Kaplan-Meier, synthetic-survival-control, or RMST proposal and no usable rejected-angle archive in the available catalogue.
The closest spectral source was stat_proxy_effectlaw_eigencollision_frontier_v1, whose solved proof separates gap-free quotient recovery from inverse-gap labeled recovery.
That source was linked to the web literature on rank-robust low-rank inference, yielding the merged shrinking-gap/rank-selection opportunity.
The strongest explicit unresolved obligation was stat_cot_boundary_degeneracy_frontier_v1/open_obligations[0], concerning observable common-multiplier calibration through covariance degeneracy.
The same stat_cot run exposed a growing-resolution obstruction: population spectral control need not yield relative Hilbert-Schmidt consistency of an observed spectrum, but that candidate was dropped as less direct than the continuous-time opportunity.
The exp_bandit_random_qv_studentization_frontier_v1 reviewer supplied a transferable warning about primitive variance nondegeneracy, but its destination was dropped as lower-value than the six retained entries.
No strengthening_paths or rejected-angle files yielded an additional topic-specific opportunity that passed the merged G1–G5 filter.
